inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 3,942.6M basic shares outstanding at 2026-08-27 (FY2026 10-K cover) + 34M dilutive potential shares (FY2026 EPS note, treasury-stock method) = ~3,977M. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution too would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense $3,830M + taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards $1,873M (XBRL PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). Cisco publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.7%; debt ~$29.5B against ~$424B market cap (~6.5% weight) at ~3.5% after tax -> ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases are immaterial for Cisco (operating lease cost well under 1% of revenue); left inside EBITDA as reported. No lease liabilities in net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1: operating company, US tech hardware/software). First valuation of CSCO; no prior DCF and no memory entry. NET DEBT: total debt $29,533M (short-term debt $10,161M incl. $6.7B commercial paper + long-term debt $19,372M, per 10-K MD&A 'Total debt') less cash, cash equivalents and investments $14,297M = $15,236M. The CSV TotalDebt of $33,033M double-counts the $3.5B current portion of long-term debt (LongTermDebt 22,872 + DebtCurrent 10,161) and was not used. Non-marketable equity investments are excluded from the bridge (conservative). INTEREST INCOME: Cisco is net-debt, so interest income ($866M FY26) is not deducted from the owner-FCF base; the component build is unlevered and cash is credited once in the bridge. OWNER FCF FY26: reported FCF $12,767M - SBC incl. withholding $5,703M = $7,064M. This base is depressed by the final $2.3B US transition-tax (TCJA) payment in FY26 and a ~$2B working-capital build for AI/hyperscaler product shipments; normalised for the transition tax it is ~$9.4B, and on an unlevered basis (adding back ~$0.5B after-tax net interest) ~$9.9B (15.6% of revenue). The component build's year-1 owner-FCF margin (~19-20%) is above that because (i) the transition tax is gone, (ii) FY27 guidance implies ~1pp non-GAAP operating margin expansion, and (iii) year-1 revenue is +15%. SBC: withholding taxes on net-share settlement ($1,873M) are elevated by the ~60% share-price rise over FY26; the forward sbc_pct path starts at 8.3% (SBC ~5.6-6% + withholding ~2.5%) rather than the 9.0% FY26 print, declining 0.1-0.2pp/yr. BUYBACKS: Cisco is a repurchaser ($6.1B FY26, $8.1B authorisation remaining) plus ~$6.5B dividends; the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention. EBITDA margin is pre-SBC but AFTER restructuring (~$0.7B/yr, recurring at Cisco for a decade), i.e. GAAP op income + D&A + SBC = 34.3% in FY26. D&A path reflects acquired-intangible amortisation rolling off (next-12-month amortisation $1,534M per 10-K). Cash tax: normalised FY26 cash tax ex transition tax ~$2.5B (~16% of GAAP pretax); FY27 guide 15% GAAP / 18.5% non-GAAP effective rate; model 17% ramping to 19%.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (4.0%) is 33% below EPS 5yr CAGR (6.0%): Cisco returns more than 100% of net income via ~$6B buybacks + ~$6.5B dividends a year, so book value understates the compounding. Revenue 5yr CAGR (4.9%) selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes): FY2021 $12,365M, FY2023 $16,087M, FY2026 $7,064M. The owner-FCF CAGR is far below the reported-FCF CAGR because SBC + withholding rose from $2.4B (FY21) to $5.7B (FY26): an increasing share of reported cash flow is paid in stock. Both endpoints are also distorted by tax timing: FY2023 FCF was inflated by the IRS disaster-relief deferral of California tax payments into FY2024, and FY2026 carries the final $2.3B TCJA transition-tax payment. Ex-transition-tax, the FY26 owner FCF is ~$9.4B (3yr CAGR -16.5%, 5yr -5.4%). Revenue includes Splunk from Q4 FY2024 (acquired March 2024, ~$28B), so FY24-26 revenue growth is partly acquired.

base.narrative: FY27 delivers guidance midpoint ($72.8B, +15%) including ~$7.5B hyperscaler AI revenue; growth then settles to 4-6% as the AI build-out normalises and the campus refresh runs its course. Margin held at FY26-FY27 level (non-GAAP op margin ~35-36%).

bull.narrative: Networking supercycle is durable: hyperscaler AI orders keep compounding beyond FY27, Silicon One wins back share in 800G/1.6T scale-out, and the security/observability (Splunk) software mix lifts margins ~2pp.

bear.narrative: FY27 falls short of guidance as hyperscaler capex digests; FY28 revenue declines as AI and campus-refresh orders pull back, and the core returns to low-single-digit growth. Arista and white-box share gains plus lower-margin AI mix and tariffs compress margin ~2.5pp.

scenario_narratives.base: Cisco converts its record order book into FY27 guidance (revenue $72.2-73.4B, non-GAAP EPS $5.05-5.11), with hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue rising from ~$4B to ~$7.5B. After FY27 the supercycle normalises rather than reverses: enterprise campus refresh, security (Splunk, Hypershield) and observability hold the business at 4-6% growth fading to 3%, and margins stay at the FY26-27 level because AI hardware mix dilution offsets software mix gains. SBC plus withholding stays ~7-8% of revenue, funded by ~$6B/yr buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI networking supercycle is durable and Cisco wins share in it: hyperscaler orders (already $9.3B in FY26) keep compounding past FY27, Silicon One and optics win 800G/1.6T scale-out and sovereign/neocloud AI builds, and enterprises re-architect campus and data-center networks for AI inference. Splunk and security become a larger, higher-margin recurring base (56% of revenue recurring, RPO $46.7B), lifting EBITDA margin ~2pp over five years. Revenue grows high-single-digit through FY30.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY26-27 surge proves to be a hyperscaler capex cycle, not a structural step-up. Arista (already ahead in 100G-800G data-center switching) and white-box/Nvidia Spectrum-X take the next generation of AI back-end networking, a handful of concentrated webscale customers pause orders and FY28 revenue falls ~4%. Lower-margin AI hardware, tariffs and restructuring disruption (~4,000 job cuts in May 2026) compress margins ~2.5pp, and the legacy switching/routing/collaboration core reverts to ~2% growth.
scenario_narratives._source: Bull/bear axes from CSCO_Analysis.json (2026-09) bull_case / bear_case / risks; guidance from the Q4 FY2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-08-12).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): an unusually large share of incremental growth depends on a few hyperscaler customers whose capex can pause quickly, and Arista leads in the AI switching segment. Base 55%: FY27 is well covered by record orders and RPO of $46.7B, and the recurring software/services half of revenue anchors the outer years. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull needs both a multi-year extension of hyperscaler AI spend AND Cisco share gains in AI back-end networking, two independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cisco is valued on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC and the cash taxes Cisco pays on net-share settlement are both treated as real costs (together ~9% of FY26 revenue), and the share count is held flat because ~$6B/yr of buybacks keeps it flat. FY27 is anchored on management's guidance; outer years fade to mature-networking growth. On this basis the market price sits above the house value and much of the way toward (or beyond) the street basis that treats SBC as non-cash: the current price is paying for the AI networking supercycle continuing beyond FY27.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hyperscaler AI order concentration: FY27 guidance includes ~$7.5B hyperscaler AI revenue that could pause quickly
Share loss to Arista / white-box / Nvidia Spectrum-X in high-speed AI data-center switching
SBC + withholding treatment: ~$5.7B/yr; the house vs street gap is ~$25-30/share
Gross-margin dilution from lower-margin AI hardware mix and tariffs
Owner-FCF base distortion: FY26 includes the final $2.3B TCJA transition-tax payment and a working-capital build; FY23 was inflated by a tax deferral
